@graph.name: Pillow Bag Case Packer
@graph.description: A pillow bag case packer is a top-load machine that loads pillow-shaped flexible bags into shipping cases in a set count and pattern, by robotic placement, by an integrated erect, pack and seal machine or by controlled gravity drop. Pillow bags are the one product that all three case packing platforms from TRF Industrial Automation pack: TRFRapidpack, TRFOnepack and TRFDroppack. The choice comes down to your line setup and speed.

mainEntity.name: Does a Pillow Bag Case Packer Need Vision-Guided Robotics?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only when bag positions vary. TRFRapidpack picks with vision-guided delta robots when bags leave the bagger in a random flow, and with indexed picking when they arrive in a controlled position. TRFDroppack collates bags before the drop and does not use robotic picking. TRF defines the approach in the application review, based on your infeed, SKU count and pattern.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Difference Between a Drop Packer and a Robotic Case Packer?

acceptedAnswer.text: A robotic case packer places each bag or group of bags in a precise position, which suits high-mix lines and fragile contents. A drop packer collates bags and loads them by controlled gravity, which suits repetitive formats with less mechanical complexity and no robotic tooling to maintain. TRF offers TRFRapidpack as the robotic option and TRFDroppack as the drop packer.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Difference Between an Integrated Case Packer and Separate Erecting, Packing and Sealing Machines?

acceptedAnswer.text: An integrated case packer erects the case, loads it and seals it in one coordinated machine, with one controls platform. Separate machines need their own interfaces, controls and floor space. TRFOnepack is the integrated option, for applications of about 20 to 50 products per minute, and it can start standalone and later join a complete TRF end-of-line system.

mainEntity.name: Can a Case Packer Handle Frozen or IQF Products?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, within the validated application. TRFDroppack packs IQF product bags and frozen food bags, and frozen food is one of the focus industries for TRFRapidpack. TRF validates the bag, the pattern and the operating conditions with real product before closing the design, and the same project can extend to palletizing below 32°F with TRFSubzero.

mainEntity.name: How Fast Can a Case Packer Change Over Between SKUs?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on how different the bags, patterns and cases are. TRFRapidpack changes products and patterns by recipe, with reduced mechanical adjustments, and TRFOnepack runs multiple recipes through robotic loading. TRFDroppack is designed for standardized patterns. During engineering, TRF defines which changes are made in software and which, if any, require a format part.

mainEntity.name: Can Case Packing Equipment Integrate With My Existing Palletizer and Conveyors?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Each TRF case packing platform can run standalone or integrate with conveyors, case handling, palletizing and intralogistics as one end-of-line system. TRFIntraflow carries sealed cases to a TRFCobot, TRFCompact or TRFSpeed palletizer, and interfaces with your bagger and existing equipment are defined during project engineering. See end-of-line integration.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Typical ROI of Switching From Manual to Robotic Case Packing?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no typical figure, because payback depends on your plant. The estimate compares the installed cost of the system with the annual savings: people packing bags by hand per shift, shifts per day, local labor cost, the extra output the bagger gains when packing stops limiting it, broken product avoided and time saved at changeovers. A TRF Sales Engineer builds it with your data.
